title: Meetings that end with decisions
performance: the viewer runs their next meeting so it ends with each decision read back and sent in writing with an owner and a date

audience.assumed_prior: knows how meetings run; has sat through many that ended without a clear outcome
audience.why: the brief's audience runs or attends recurring team and project meetings
audience.motivation: wants less time lost and to know what was agreed and who does what next
audience.context: busy working adults, watching between tasks, with sound and captions

strategy.name: worked_example_led
strategy.rationale: the knowledge sheet is a procedure in time order (before, during, close: F1 to F13); one meeting run through those steps shows the whole method before each step is named
strategy.signature_move: run the step in Sam's meeting on the board, show what changes, then name the step and add it to the growing list

misconceptions.belief: an agenda topic such as 'Pilot update' is enough to set up a decision
misconceptions.why_tempting: it names the subject everyone will talk about, so it feels like preparation

misconceptions.belief: a line like 'Discussed the pilot timeline' in the notes means something was decided
misconceptions.why_tempting: it records that the meeting covered the subject, which feels like progress

hook.sketch: An hour of good discussion. Everyone leaves, and nobody can say what was decided, or who does what next.

arc.promise: three moves, before, during and at the close, that make the same meeting end with decisions
arc.bridge_from_prior: the viewer's own recurring meeting: Sam's weekly project meeting stands in for it

sections.goal: the viewer can use a question in the invite to name the decision a meeting must make, and choose who must attend
the viewer can carry out the opening moves of the meeting: restate the decision, park side topics, and say how and by whom it is decided
the viewer can distinguish a recorded decision (what, owner, date) from a topic discussed, and close by reading decisions back and sending them

arc.payoff: Sam's same meeting ends with three lines read back and sent that afternoon: what was decided, who owns it, by when.

practice_ladder.what: Sam's meeting rewritten step by step on the board, every step narrated
the viewer judges two lines of Sam's closing notes before the answer is shown
the viewer rewrites the first line of their own next agenda as a decision question

slowdown_at: what makes a line a decision

recall_moments.prompt_sketch: Two lines from Sam's notes: 'Discussed the pilot timeline' and 'Pilot ships in June, owner Priya, plan by Friday'. Which one is a decision?
recall_moments.answer: the second: it says what was decided, who owns it and by when
recall_moments.tempting_wrong: the first names the subject and sounds like progress, but it records only a topic discussed, with no decision, owner or date (F12)

transfer_tasks: before your next meeting, rewrite the first line of its agenda as the decision it must make, phrased as a question

persona.voice: a capable colleague who has sat through too many meetings, brisk and practical
persona.delivery_notes: dry and brisk on the problem, a short pause before the quiz answer, slower and warmer on the closing read-back

gagne.attention: hook: the meeting with no outcome
gagne.recall_prior: bridge: the viewer's own recurring meeting
gagne.present: S1 to S3 in time order
gagne.guidance: signature move: run the step, then name it on the growing list
gagne.feedback: quiz answer explained, with why the topic line tempts
gagne.assess: the quiz on Sam's closing notes
gagne.transfer: transfer task: rewrite your next agenda's first line

merrill.problem_centered: Sam's meeting is the running problem from hook to payoff
merrill.activation: the hook draws on the viewer's own meetings
merrill.demonstration: S1 and S2 show each step in Sam's meeting before naming it
merrill.application: the S3 quiz makes the viewer judge the notes
merrill.integration: payoff and transfer task hand the method back

mayer.coherence: one running example, no side stories, no statistics
mayer.signalling: one slowdown, on what makes a line a decision
mayer.redundancy: the board shows short labels; narration explains
mayer.contiguity: each step is drawn as it is spoken
mayer.segmenting: three short sections, one moment each
mayer.pre_training: the hook shows the meeting before any step is named

arcs.attention: the familiar meeting that ends with nothing
arcs.confidence: three small steps on a list that grows
arcs.satisfaction: the payoff returns to Sam's meeting, solved
